tc_derrida.cite: Derrida, The random energy model, Physics Reports 67, 29-35 (1980), Sec. 4: 'T_c = J/2 sqrt(log 2)' with P(E) = (pi N J^2)^(-1/2) exp(-E^2/(N J^2)), Eq. (2); read from the copy at thp.uni-koeln.de/krug/teaching-Dateien/WS2011/Derrida1980.pdf. Same statement in Derrida & Mottishaw, J. Stat. Mech. (2015) P01021, doi:10.1088/1742-5468/2015/01/P01021, arXiv:1410.1432, Eq. (2). Full paper Derrida, Phys. Rev. B 24, 2613 (1981), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.24.2613 (not fetched). The paper states the closed form; value = its decimal at J = 1 (replicant N_scale = J^2/2 = 1/2)
tc_derrida.independent_route: Derrida's microcanonical argument redone numerically: root e0 < 0 of replicant's s(e) = ln 2 - e^2/(2 N_scale) and the slope s'(e0) = beta_c (tests, three N_scale values); plus the exact finite-N quenched E ln Z by quadrature (no replicas), which follows the frozen branch above beta_c

ground_energy_derrida.cite: Derrida, Physics Reports 67, 29 (1980), Sec. 5: for T < T_c 'the system is frozen in its ground state and the energy is E = -N J sqrt(log 2)'; also Derrida & Mottishaw, arXiv:1410.1432, Eq. (3). Closed form, decimal at J = 1. In the frozen phase f = E_ground / N (entropy 0)
ground_energy_derrida.independent_route: replicant's 1RSB route (rem_1rsb: n/m groups of m coincident replicas, m* = beta_c/beta) gives -beta f = beta sqrt(2 N_scale ln 2), equal to -beta * (-sqrt(ln 2)) at N_scale = 1/2; the exact finite-N quenched quadrature approaches it as N grows

m_times_beta_over_beta_c.cite: Derrida & Mottishaw, J. Stat. Mech. (2015) P01021, arXiv:1410.1432, Eqs. (4)-(6): Parisi q(x) = Theta(x - 1 + <P2>) with <P2> = 1 - mu, mu = T/T_c below T_c, so the 1RSB breakpoint is m = T/T_c = beta_c/beta; same in Derrida & Mottishaw, J. Phys. A 55 (2022), doi:10.1088/1751-8121/ac71e9, arXiv:2202.12584, Eq. (5) (<Y_2> = 1 - beta_c/beta). Meaning: m * beta / beta_c = 1 for beta >= beta_c
m_times_beta_over_beta_c.independent_route: replicant derives m* symbolically: -beta f(m) = ln 2 / m + N_scale beta^2 m / 2, the energy part from ansatz.sum_offdiag_power (q in {0, 1}) with ansatz.n_to_zero, the entropy part from (2^N)^(n/m) block choices; sympy solves d/dm = 0 to sqrt(2 ln 2 / N_scale)/beta

participation_ratio_kz1539_beta3.cite: F. Krzakala & L. Zdeborova, 'Statistical Physics Methods in Optimization and Machine Learning: An Introduction to Replica, Cavity & Message-Passing techniques', lecture notes, version of June 9 2024 (the PDF read page by page and as text), Sec. 15.2.4, Eq. (15.39) (p. 229; notes.txt lines 14042-14112): 'EY = 1 - m = 1 - beta_c/beta' (printed, a replica 1RSB result, physics-level); the value is its evaluation at beta = 3, mpmath at 50 digits rounded to 30. KZ p. 230 says the participation ratio 'diverges' at T_c: Y -> 0 there, its inverse (the quantity plotted in Fig. 15.2.1) diverges. Convention: KZ Eq. (15.1), P(E) = N(0, N/2), is replicant's N_scale = 1/2 (beta_c = 2 sqrt(ln 2)); m = beta_c/beta; banked at beta = 3 (m = 0.5550364...).
participation_ratio_kz1539_beta3.independent_route: exact REM sampling (2^14 i.i.d. energies over seeds 0-399, the Gibbs weights) and the exact finite-N moment E[Y] = int du 2^N E[x^2 e^-x] (E e^-x)^(2^N - 1) by quadrature (families/rem.py, no replicas): the sampled 99% band contains the exact finite-N value and lies within the declared finite-N systematic 0.035 of 1 - m at N = 14, beta = 4 beta_c (tests/test_rem_condensation.py); Derrida & Mottishaw, arXiv:1410.1432, Eqs. (4)-(6) (<P2> = 1 - mu, read for the m_times_beta_over_beta_c key)

participation_ratio_sq_kz1566_beta3.cite: F. Krzakala & L. Zdeborova, 'Statistical Physics Methods in Optimization and Machine Learning: An Introduction to Replica, Cavity & Message-Passing techniques', lecture notes, version of June 9 2024 (the PDF read page by page and as text), Exercise 15.2, Eq. (15.66) (p. 234; notes.txt lines 14357-14367): 'E[Y^2] = (3 - 5m + 2m^2)/3' for beta >= beta_c (printed as an exercise result, replica, physics-level); the value is its evaluation at beta = 3, mpmath at 50 digits rounded to 30. Convention: KZ Eq. (15.1), P(E) = N(0, N/2), is replicant's N_scale = 1/2 (beta_c = 2 sqrt(ln 2)); m = beta_c/beta; banked at beta = 3 (m = 0.5550364...).
participation_ratio_sq_kz1566_beta3.independent_route: exact REM sampling over named seeds and the exact finite-N E[Y^2] = int du [2^N B4 g^(2^N - 1) + 2^N (2^N - 1) B2^2 g^(2^N - 2)]/6 by quadrature (families/rem.py): band, exact value and (15.66) agree within the declared 0.035 at N = 14, beta = 4 beta_c (tests/test_rem_condensation.py); E[Y^2] > E[Y]^2 (not self-averaging)
